\section*{How to use this dictionary}
Keep it open next to the manual (\href{simplydata_manual.pdf}{\code{simplydata\_\allowbreak{}manual.\allowbreak{}pdf}}). The first pages,
\hyperref[glance]{\textbf{All the words at a glance}}, show every word group by group, one line
each; the entries A to Z after them explain each word in full.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=1.6em]
  \item \textbf{Look up a word.} The words are in A to Z order. The words at the top of each page
    are the first and the last word on that page, as in a printed dictionary.
  \item \textbf{Read what it means.} One line says what the word does, in the words of
    \code{sdata.help("word")}.
  \item \textbf{Try the example.} Every example runs as written. Most use a practice table, named
    in brackets after the example: \code{(marks)} means
    \code{table = sdata.table(sdata.get\_example("marks"))} for a table word, or
    \code{chart = sdata.chart(sdata.get\_example("marks"))} for a chart word.
  \item \textbf{See what runs underneath.} \textbf{Underneath} names the package that does the work
    (pandas, Polars, NumPy, seaborn, SciPy, R ...). Where the manual has a grey box ``The same
    underneath'', the line is read from its tested code, and the box shows the full code.
  \item \textbf{Read the page.} \textbf{Manual p.} gives the page of the manual where the word is
    explained in full; the number is a link that opens the manual at that page. \textbf{Lesson}
    gives the lessons that teach it.
\end{enumerate}
Some words belong to more than one thing: \code{save} saves a chart, a table or numbers. Then
the word has one entry with a part for each, marked
\kind{chart}, \kind{table}, \kind{nums} and so on:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}ll@{}}
\kind{sdata} \code{sdata.chart(...)} & called on simplydata itself\\
\kind{table} \code{table.keep\_rows\_where(...)} & a step on a table\\
\kind{chart} \code{chart.draw\_bars(...)} & a step on a chart\\
\kind{option} \code{show="median"} & an option inside a chart step\\
\kind{nums} \code{nums.find\_average()} & a step on numbers: \code{nums = sdata.numbers([12, 15, 9])}\\
\kind{grid} \code{grid.get\_row(1)} & a step on a grid: \code{grid = sdata.number\_grid([[3, 5], [8, 6]])}\\
\kind{dist} \code{dist.find\_chance\_that\_value(is\_above=60)} & a step on a distribution: \code{dist = sdata.distribution("normal")}\\
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Know the name from pandas, R, NumPy or matplotlib (\code{groupby}, \code{iloc}, \code{hist},
\code{curve\_fit})? Look it up in \hyperref[other:names]{\textbf{Coming from another tool?}} at the end.

\section*{How the words are built}
A line of simplydata reads like an instruction you say to the program: the thing, then what it
should do, then the details: \code{table.keep\_rows\_where("marks", is\_above=50)},
\code{chart.draw\_bars(x="class", y="marks")}.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.2em]
  \item \textbf{A word starts with what it does, in full English words}: \code{keep\_rows\_where},
    \code{find\_average\_of}, \code{draw\_bars}, \code{write\_title\_on\_top}. No short forms to remember.
  \item \textbf{Words come in families.} Learn \code{keep\_rows\_where} and you can guess
    \code{keep\_columns}, \code{keep\_each\_number\_that} and \code{keep\_first\_rows}. \hyperref[families]{Word families}
    lists them.
  \item \textbf{A small word joins the first input}: \code{keep\_rows\_where("marks", ...)},
    \code{fill\_empty\_cells\_in("price", ...)}, \code{find\_average\_of("marks")}.
  \item \textbf{Anything for one axis ends in \code{\_x} or \code{\_y}}: \code{label\_y},
    \code{set\_range\_x}, \code{use\_log\_scale\_y}. x goes across, y goes up.
  \item \textbf{One option name means one thing everywhere}: \code{for\_each\_group\_in=} (a result for each
    group of a table), \code{in\_each="row"} (a result for each row of a grid), conditions start with \code{is\_} (\code{is\_above=}, \code{is\_between=[low, high]}),
    \code{colour=}, \code{from\_column=}.
  \item \textbf{Counting starts at 1}, as people count: \code{nums.get\_number\_at(1)} is the first number,
    \code{grid.get\_row(1)} the top row.
  \item \textbf{Every change can be taken back} with \code{undo()}.
\end{itemize}

\clearpage\section*{All the words at a glance}\label{glance}\markboth{At a glance}{At a glance}
Every word, group by group, in the order \code{sdata.show\_all\_words()} prints them. Table words
are steps on a table, for looking at data, cleaning it and summing it up; chart words are steps on
a chart; number words are steps on a list (or a grid) of numbers:
{\footnotesize\begin{verbatim}
import simplydata as sdata
table = sdata.table(sdata.get_example("marks"))   # or sdata.table("my_file.xlsx")
table.keep_rows_where("marks", is_above=50)
table.find_average_of("marks", for_each_group_in="class")   # says the answer in a sentence
table.save("good_marks.xlsx")
chart = table.start_chart()             # or sdata.chart(table), sdata.chart("my_file.xlsx")
chart.draw_bars(x="class", y="marks", error="standard error")
chart.write_title_on_top("Good marks")
chart.save("marks.png")
nums = sdata.numbers([12, 15, 9, 20, 14])
bigger = nums * 2                       # symbols make new numbers
nums.keep_each_number_that(is_above=10) # words change the numbers (undo() takes it back)
nums.find_average()
grid = sdata.number_grid([[3, 5, 2], [8, 6, 4]])
\end{verbatim}}
Every example runs as written on the practice table in brackets after it: \code{(weather)} means
\code{weather = sdata.get\_example("weather")}, then \code{chart = sdata.chart(weather)} for a chart
word or \code{table = sdata.table(weather)} for a table word. Number words use
\code{nums = sdata.numbers([12, 15, 9, 20, 14])}, grid words
\code{grid = sdata.number\_grid([[3, 5, 2], [8, 6, 4]])} and system words
\code{system = sdata.system("1 / (s**2 + 2*s + 5)")}. Steps such as \code{fit\_line} or
\code{write\_title\_on\_top} go after a chart step such as \code{chart.draw\_dots(...)}, and \code{a},
\code{b} in \code{sdata.put\_side\_by\_side(a, b)} are charts you made first. Each word is a link to its
entry, and \code{sdata.help("word")} shows its example ready to run.

\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:draw-polar]{\code{draw\_\allowbreak{}polar}}}{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}draw\_\allowbreak{}polar(angle=\textquotedbl{}wind\_\allowbreak{}direction\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} distance=\textquotedbl{}wind\_\allowbreak{}speed\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} colour=\textquotedbl{}city\textquotedbl{})}}{Dots on a round chart: how far round, and how far out.}

\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:draw-surface]{\code{draw\_\allowbreak{}surface}}}{\code{chart.\allowbreak{}draw\_\allowbreak{}surface(x=\textquotedbl{}east\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} y=\textquotedbl{}north\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} z=\textquotedbl{}height\textquotedbl{})}}{A 3D landscape: \code{z=} is how high the ground is.}

\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-cut-off]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}cut\_\allowbreak{}off}}}{\code{dist.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}cut\_\allowbreak{}off(with\_\allowbreak{}chance\_\allowbreak{}above=0.\allowbreak{}025)}}{The value with this chance above it (or below it): critical values.}

\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-average]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}average}}}{\code{dist.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}average()}}{The average (mean) of the distribution.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-median]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}median}}}{\code{dist.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}median()}}{The median: half of the distribution is below it.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-standard-deviation]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}standard\_\allowbreak{}deviation}}}{\code{dist.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}standard\_\allowbreak{}deviation()}}{The standard deviation of the distribution.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-variance]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}variance}}}{\code{dist.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}variance()}}{The variance (the standard deviation squared).}

\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-columns-that-predict]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}that\_\allowbreak{}predict}}}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}that\_\allowbreak{}predict(\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} using=[\textquotedbl{}hours\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}sleep\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}breakfast\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}class\textquotedbl{}])}}{Choose the columns that predict a column, with the lasso and a penalty checked on left-out rows.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-group-levels-of]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}group\_\allowbreak{}levels\_\allowbreak{}of}}}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}group\_\allowbreak{}levels\_\allowbreak{}of(\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} using=[\textquotedbl{}hours\textquotedbl{}],\allowbreak{} grouped\_\allowbreak{}by=\textquotedbl{}school\textquotedbl{})}}{Each group's own starting level (and own slope) in a mixed model.}

\textquotedbl{}x5\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}x6\textquotedbl{}],\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}speed\textquotedbl{}: [\textquotedbl{}x7\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}x8\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} \textquotedbl{}x9\textquotedbl{}]\})}}{Check a model of hidden factors you wrote down beforehand: does it match the data?}

(Cox model, hazard ratios)}

\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:times]{\code{times}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}times(2)}}{Multiply every number by a number.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:divide-by]{\code{divide\_\allowbreak{}by}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}divide\_\allowbreak{}by(4)}}{Divide every number by a number.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:raise-to-power]{\code{raise\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}power}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}raise\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}power(2)}}{Raise every number to a power: \code{raise\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}power(2)} squares, \code{raise\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}power(3)} cubes.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:take-square-root]{\code{take\_\allowbreak{}square\_\allowbreak{}root}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}take\_\allowbreak{}square\_\allowbreak{}root()}}{The square root of every number: 9 becomes 3.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:take-absolute-value]{\code{take\_\allowbreak{}absolute\_\allowbreak{}value}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}take\_\allowbreak{}absolute\_\allowbreak{}value()}}{Every number without its minus sign: -3 becomes 3.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:round-to]{\code{round\_\allowbreak{}to}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}round\_\allowbreak{}to(2)}}{Round every number to this many decimal places.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:take-log]{\code{take\_\allowbreak{}log}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}take\_\allowbreak{}log()}}{The logarithm of every number: natural (base e) unless you give \code{base=10} or \code{base=2}.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:take-exp]{\code{take\_\allowbreak{}exp}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}take\_\allowbreak{}exp()}}{e (about 2.718) to the power of every number; it undoes \code{take\_\allowbreak{}log()}.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:turn-into-running-total]{\code{turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}running\_\allowbreak{}total}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}running\_\allowbreak{}total()}}{Each number becomes the total so far (the cumulative sum): 1, 2, 3 becomes 1, 3, 6.}
\glancegroup{Numbers: choose, sort and fill}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:keep-each-number-that]{\code{keep\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that(is\_\allowbreak{}above=50)}}{Keep only the numbers that match one condition.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:remove-each-number-that]{\code{remove\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that(is\_\allowbreak{}below=0)}}{Remove the numbers that match one condition (the opposite of \code{keep\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that}).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:keep-first-numbers]{\code{keep\_\allowbreak{}first\_\allowbreak{}numbers}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}first\_\allowbreak{}numbers(10)}}{Keep only the first numbers.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:keep-last-numbers]{\code{keep\_\allowbreak{}last\_\allowbreak{}numbers}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}last\_\allowbreak{}numbers(10)}}{Keep only the last numbers.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:keep-random-numbers]{\code{keep\_\allowbreak{}random\_\allowbreak{}numbers}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}random\_\allowbreak{}numbers(10,\allowbreak{} with\_\allowbreak{}seed=1)}}{Keep some numbers picked at random (they keep their order); a seed gives the same pick every time.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:remove-duplicate-numbers]{\code{remove\_\allowbreak{}duplicate\_\allowbreak{}numbers}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}duplicate\_\allowbreak{}numbers()}}{Remove numbers that repeat an earlier number, so each number is left once, in its first place.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:remove-empty-numbers]{\code{remove\_\allowbreak{}empty\_\allowbreak{}numbers}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}empty\_\allowbreak{}numbers()}}{Remove the empty (missing) values.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:keep-numbers-by-position]{\code{keep\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(2,\allowbreak{} to=4)}}{Keep numbers by their position, counting from 1: a run, every n-th number, or a list.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:remove-numbers-by-position]{\code{remove\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}numbers\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(\textquotedbl{}last\textquotedbl{})}}{Remove numbers by their position, counting from 1: a run, every n-th number, or a list.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:replace-each-number-that]{\code{replace\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}replace\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that(-999,\allowbreak{} with\_\allowbreak{}value=None)}}{Replace a number, or every number that meets one condition; \code{with\_\allowbreak{}value=None} makes them empty.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:fill-empty-numbers]{\code{fill\_\allowbreak{}empty\_\allowbreak{}numbers}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}fill\_\allowbreak{}empty\_\allowbreak{}numbers(with\_\allowbreak{}value=0)}}{Fill the empty values with a number, or with the average, median, value above or value below.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:sort]{\code{sort}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}sort(biggest\_\allowbreak{}first=True)}}{Put the numbers in order, smallest first; empty values go last.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:reverse]{\code{reverse}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}reverse()}}{Turn the order round: the last number comes first.}
\glancegroup{Numbers: summaries}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-average]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}average}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}average()}}{The average (mean) of the numbers; empty values are skipped.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-median]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}median}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}median()}}{The middle number once the numbers are sorted; empty values are skipped.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-total]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}total}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}total()}}{All the numbers added up; empty values are skipped.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-smallest]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}smallest}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}smallest()}}{The smallest number; empty values are skipped.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-biggest]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}biggest}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}biggest()}}{The biggest number; empty values are skipped.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-standard-deviation]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}standard\_\allowbreak{}deviation}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}standard\_\allowbreak{}deviation()}}{How spread out the numbers are: the sample standard deviation (divide by n - 1).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-percentile]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}percentile}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}percentile(90)}}{The number that this percent of the numbers are below: \code{find\_\allowbreak{}percentile(50)} is the median.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:count-each]{\code{count\_\allowbreak{}each}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}count\_\allowbreak{}each()}}{Each different number, how many times it appears, and its percent, as a table.}
\glancegroup{Grids of numbers}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:number-grid]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}grid}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}grid([[1,\allowbreak{} 2,\allowbreak{} 3],\allowbreak{} [4,\allowbreak{} 5,\allowbreak{} 6]])}}{Make a grid of numbers in rows and columns.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:make-number-grid]{\code{make\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}grid}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}grid(columns=3)}}{Make a NEW grid from these numbers, filled row by row.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:count-rows]{\code{count\_\allowbreak{}rows}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}count\_\allowbreak{}rows()}}{How many rows the grid has.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:count-columns]{\code{count\_\allowbreak{}columns}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}count\_\allowbreak{}columns()}}{How many columns the grid has.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:find-shape]{\code{find\_\allowbreak{}shape}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}shape()}}{How many rows and columns, as (rows, columns).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-first-rows]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}first\_\allowbreak{}rows}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}first\_\allowbreak{}rows(5)}}{Show the first rows.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-last-rows]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}last\_\allowbreak{}rows}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}last\_\allowbreak{}rows(5)}}{Show the last rows.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:get-number-at]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}at}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}at(row=1,\allowbreak{} column=2)}}{The number at a row and column, counting from 1.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:get-row]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}row}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}row(1)}}{One row of the grid as new numbers, counting from 1: \code{get\_\allowbreak{}row(1)} is the top row.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:get-column]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}column}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}column(1)}}{One column of the grid as new numbers, counting from 1: \code{get\_\allowbreak{}column(1)} is the left one.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:get-all-numbers]{\code{get\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}numbers}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}get\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}numbers()}}{All the numbers of the grid as a list, row by row (flatten).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:keep-rows-by-position]{\code{keep\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(1,\allowbreak{} to=2)}}{Keep rows of the grid by their position, counting from 1: a run, every n-th row, or a list.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:keep-columns-by-position]{\code{keep\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}keep\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(2,\allowbreak{} to=3)}}{Keep columns of the grid by their position, counting from 1 at the left.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:remove-rows-by-position]{\code{remove\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(1)}}{Remove rows of the grid by their position, counting from 1.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:remove-columns-by-position]{\code{remove\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}remove\_\allowbreak{}columns\_\allowbreak{}by\_\allowbreak{}position(1)}}{Remove columns of the grid by their position, counting from 1 at the left.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:replace-each-number-that]{\code{replace\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}replace\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}number\_\allowbreak{}that(is\_\allowbreak{}below=4,\allowbreak{} with\_\allowbreak{}value=0)}}{Replace a number, or every number that meets one condition; the grid keeps its rows and columns.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:swap-rows-and-columns]{\code{swap\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}and\_\allowbreak{}columns}}}{\code{grid.\allowbreak{}swap\_\allowbreak{}rows\_\allowbreak{}and\_\allowbreak{}columns()}}{Turn rows into columns and columns into rows (the transpose in maths).}
\glancegroup{Numbers: undo and finish}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:undo]{\code{undo}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}undo()}}{Take the last step back.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-steps]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}steps}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}steps()}}{List every step you did, in order.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:start-again]{\code{start\_\allowbreak{}again}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}again()}}{Go back to the numbers as they were at the start.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:turn-into-table]{\code{turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}table}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}turn\_\allowbreak{}into\_\allowbreak{}table(name=\textquotedbl{}marks\textquotedbl{})}}{Turn the numbers into a simplydata table.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:start-chart]{\code{start\_\allowbreak{}chart}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}chart()}}{Start a chart from these numbers.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:save]{\code{save}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}save(\textquotedbl{}nums.\allowbreak{}csv\textquotedbl{})}}{Save the numbers; the end of the file name decides the type.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:as-numpy]{\code{as\_\allowbreak{}numpy}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}as\_\allowbreak{}numpy()}}{Give back the numbers as a plain NumPy array, for other Python tools.}
\glancegroup{Waves and systems}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:convolve-with]{\code{convolve\_\allowbreak{}with}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}convolve\_\allowbreak{}with([1,\allowbreak{} 2,\allowbreak{} 1])}}{Convolve the numbers with other numbers: each result is a sum of products as one list slides along.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:deconvolve-by]{\code{deconvolve\_\allowbreak{}by}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}deconvolve\_\allowbreak{}by([1,\allowbreak{} 2,\allowbreak{} 3])}}{Undo a convolution: the numbers divided by other numbers (polynomial division).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:change-time-step]{\code{change\_\allowbreak{}time\_\allowbreak{}step}}}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}change\_\allowbreak{}time\_\allowbreak{}step(to=0.\allowbreak{}01,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}001)}}{Change the time between readings (resample): fewer readings (with a filter first) or more.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:make-wave]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}wave}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}wave(\textquotedbl{}sine\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} frequency=5,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}01,\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=100)}}{Numbers that make a wave: a sine, square, sawtooth, chirp, pulse or impulse.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:make-window-shape]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}window\_\allowbreak{}shape}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}window\_\allowbreak{}shape(\textquotedbl{}hann\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=64)}}{The weights of a window (taper), such as \code{\textquotedbl{}hann\textquotedbl{}}: high in the middle, low at the ends.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:system]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}system}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / (s**2 + 2*s + 5)\textquotedbl{})}}{A linear system (one input, one output) from its formula, coefficients, poles or matrices.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:step-response]{\code{step\_\allowbreak{}response}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}step\_\allowbreak{}response(until=10)}}{How the output answers an input that jumps from 0 to 1 and stays there.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:impulse-response]{\code{impulse\_\allowbreak{}response}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}impulse\_\allowbreak{}response(until=10)}}{How the output answers a short kick at time 0 (an impulse of size 1).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:response-to]{\code{response\_\allowbreak{}to}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}response\_\allowbreak{}to(sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}wave(\textquotedbl{}square\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} frequency=0.\allowbreak{}2,\allowbreak{} time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}05,\allowbreak{} how\_\allowbreak{}many=400))}}{How the output answers any input you give: a simulation.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:frequency-response]{\code{frequency\_\allowbreak{}response}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}frequency\_\allowbreak{}response(between=[0.\allowbreak{}1,\allowbreak{} 100])}}{How much the system passes each frequency (gain) and how much it delays it (phase): the Bode data.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:poles]{\code{poles}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}poles()}}{The poles: the values of s (or z) where the bottom of the formula is 0. They set how it moves.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:zeros]{\code{zeros}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}zeros()}}{The zeros: the values of s (or z) where the top of the formula is 0 (inputs that do not get through).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:is-stable]{\code{is\_\allowbreak{}stable}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}is\_\allowbreak{}stable()}}{True when every response to a bounded input stays bounded (and settles).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:steady-gain]{\code{steady\_\allowbreak{}gain}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}steady\_\allowbreak{}gain()}}{Where the output settles for a constant input of 1 (the DC gain).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:in-steps]{\code{in\_\allowbreak{}steps}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}in\_\allowbreak{}steps(time\_\allowbreak{}step=0.\allowbreak{}1)}}{The same system in steps of \code{time\_\allowbreak{}step} (discrete time), for a computer that reads and acts in steps.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:then]{\code{then}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}then(sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / s\textquotedbl{}))}}{This system, then another one after it (in series): the output of this one feeds the other.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:add]{\code{add}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}add(sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / (s + 3)\textquotedbl{}))}}{This system and another side by side, their outputs added (in parallel): both get the same input.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:with-feedback]{\code{with\_\allowbreak{}feedback}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}with\_\allowbreak{}feedback()}}{The closed loop: the output is fed back (through a sensor, say) and taken from the input.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:table]{\code{table}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}table()}}{The system as numbers: \code{form=\textquotedbl{}transfer function\textquotedbl{}} (the coefficients of the top and the bottom, highest power first: power of s (power of z in steps), numerator, denominator), \code{\textquotedbl{}state space\textquotedbl{}} (the matrices A, B, C, D in controller form: matrix, row, column, value; SciPy tf2ss, as R control::tf2ss) or \code{\textquotedbl{}poles and zeros\textquotedbl{}} (kind, real part, imaginary part; the last row is the gain).}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:chart]{\code{chart}}}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}chart()}}{A chart of the system: \code{show=\textquotedbl{}bode\textquotedbl{}} (gain in decibels and phase against frequency on a log scale, two panels; \code{\textquotedbl{}gain and phase\textquotedbl{}} is accepted), \code{\textquotedbl{}step\textquotedbl{}}, \code{\textquotedbl{}impulse\textquotedbl{}}, \code{\textquotedbl{}poles and zeros\textquotedbl{}} (x for poles, o for zeros; the unit circle for a system in steps; \code{\textquotedbl{}pole-zero\textquotedbl{}} is accepted) or \code{\textquotedbl{}nyquist\textquotedbl{}} (the frequency response as one curve; a feedback loop is stable when it stays clear of -1).}
\glancegroup{Help}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-all-words]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}words}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}all\_\allowbreak{}words()}}{Print every simplydata word with a short example.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:help]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}help}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}help(\textquotedbl{}draw\_\allowbreak{}bars\textquotedbl{})}}{Explain one word: what it does, its options and an example you can run.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-lesson]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}lesson}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}lesson(1)}}{A lesson: an example to run, what each line does, and a task.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-packages-used]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}packages\_\allowbreak{}used}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}packages\_\allowbreak{}used()}}{List the packages that did the work behind your simplydata words, and how to cite them.}
\glancegroup{30 days of simplydata}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:start-30-days]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}30\_\allowbreak{}days}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}start\_\allowbreak{}30\_\allowbreak{}days()}}{Start 30 days of simplydata: an hour a day of warm-up questions, lessons and tasks.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-today]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}today}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}today()}}{Show today's day of the 30 days of simplydata: warm-up questions, what to do and a task.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-day]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}day}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}day(5)}}{Show any day of the 30 days, without changing where you are.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:show-answers]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}answers}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}show\_\allowbreak{}answers(5)}}{The answers to a day's warm-up questions, and a worked answer to its task.}
\glanceword{\hyperref[dict:go-to-next-day]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}go\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}next\_\allowbreak{}day}}}{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}go\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}next\_\allowbreak{}day()}}{Go on to the next day now, without waiting for tomorrow.}
\end{glancetable}

\clearpage\section*{Word families}\label{families}\markboth{Word families}{Word families}
A family is learned once and used again and again: the start or the end of a word says what kind of thing it does. Each family below lists its words; each word is a link to its entry.

\wordfamily{...\_x and ...\_y}{a chart word for one axis: x goes across, y goes up}{\hyperref[dict:add-second-y]{\code{add\_\allowbreak{}second\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:draw-line-at-x]{\code{draw\_\allowbreak{}line\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:draw-line-at-y]{\code{draw\_\allowbreak{}line\_\allowbreak{}at\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:flip-x]{\code{flip\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:flip-y]{\code{flip\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:label-x]{\code{label\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:label-y]{\code{label\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:order-x]{\code{order\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:order-y]{\code{order\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:put-ticks-x]{\code{put\_\allowbreak{}ticks\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:put-ticks-y]{\code{put\_\allowbreak{}ticks\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:rotate-labels-x]{\code{rotate\_\allowbreak{}labels\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:rotate-labels-y]{\code{rotate\_\allowbreak{}labels\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:set-range-x]{\code{set\_\allowbreak{}range\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:set-range-y]{\code{set\_\allowbreak{}range\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:shade-between-x]{\code{shade\_\allowbreak{}between\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:shade-between-y]{\code{shade\_\allowbreak{}between\_\allowbreak{}y}}, \hyperref[dict:use-log-scale-x]{\code{use\_\allowbreak{}log\_\allowbreak{}scale\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:use-log-scale-y]{\code{use\_\allowbreak{}log\_\allowbreak{}scale\_\allowbreak{}y}}}
\wordfamily{shade\_...}{shades a band across the chart}{\hyperref[dict:shade-between-x]{\code{shade\_\allowbreak{}between\_\allowbreak{}x}}, \hyperref[dict:shade-between-y]{\code{shade\_\allowbreak{}between\_\allowbreak{}y}}}
\wordfamily{as\_...}{hands the data on to another library}{\hyperref[dict:as-numpy]{\code{as\_\allowbreak{}numpy}}, \hyperref[dict:as-pandas]{\code{as\_\allowbreak{}pandas}}, \hyperref[dict:as-polars]{\code{as\_\allowbreak{}polars}}}
\wordfamily{undo, show\_steps, start\_again}{every change can be taken back}{\hyperref[dict:show-steps]{\code{show\_\allowbreak{}steps}}, \hyperref[dict:start-again]{\code{start\_\allowbreak{}again}}, \hyperref[dict:undo]{\code{undo}}}
\end{familytable}

\section*{The words, A to Z}\label{words}
\begin{dictcolumns}
\letterhead{A}
\headword{add}{dict:add}
\sense{nums}{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}add()}}
\means{Add a number to every number (or add numbers one by one).}
\eg{\code{nums.\allowbreak{}add(5)}}
\field{Options}{\code{number=}}
\field{Underneath}{NumPy}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:subtract]{\code{subtract}}, \hyperref[dict:times]{\code{times}}, \hyperref[dict:divide-by]{\code{divide\_\allowbreak{}by}}, \hyperref[dict:raise-to-power]{\code{raise\_\allowbreak{}to\_\allowbreak{}power}}, \hyperref[dict:take-square-root]{\code{take\_\allowbreak{}square\_\allowbreak{}root}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:nums.add}{515}{section*.376}; lesson 13 (\manualpage{lesson:13}{81}{chapter.II.13})}
\sense{system}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}add()}}
\means{This system and another side by side, their outputs added (in parallel): both get the same input.}
\eg{\code{system.\allowbreak{}add(sdata.\allowbreak{}system(\textquotedbl{}1 / (s + 3)\textquotedbl{}))}}
\field{Options}{\code{other}}
\field{Underneath}{SciPy (signal.lti / dlti, step, impulse, lsim, freqresp, freqz, cont2discrete, tf2ss, tf2zpk); the formula read with Python's ast and NumPy polynomials; rise time, settling time, overshoot and margins from python-control (\code{step\_\allowbreak{}info}, \code{stability\_\allowbreak{}margins}: simplydata[systems])}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:then]{\code{then}}, \hyperref[dict:with-feedback]{\code{with\_\allowbreak{}feedback}}, \hyperref[dict:in-steps]{\code{in\_\allowbreak{}steps}}, \hyperref[dict:table]{\code{table}}, \hyperref[dict:steady-gain]{\code{steady\_\allowbreak{}gain}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:system.add}{545}{section*.453}}
\headword{add\_adjusted\_p\_value\_column}{dict:add-adjusted-p-value-column}
\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}adjusted\_\allowbreak{}p\_\allowbreak{}value\_\allowbreak{}column()}}
\means{Adjust p-values for testing many things at once, in a new column.}
\eg{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}adjusted\_\allowbreak{}p\_\allowbreak{}value\_\allowbreak{}column(\textquotedbl{}p\_\allowbreak{}adjusted\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} test\_\allowbreak{}method=\textquotedbl{}benjamini-hochberg\textquotedbl{})}}
\field{Options}{\code{name=}, \code{from\_\allowbreak{}column=}, \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}}
\field{Other tools}{\code{fdr}, \code{lfdr}, \code{local\_\allowbreak{}fdr}, \code{multipletests}, \code{p\_\allowbreak{}adjust}, \code{q\_\allowbreak{}values}, \code{qvalue}, \code{qvalues}, \code{storey}}
\field{Underneath}{statsmodels (stats.multitest.multipletests: Holm, Bonferroni, Benjamini-Hochberg, Benjamini-Yekutieli, Hochberg and Hommel, as R \code{p.\allowbreak{}adjust()}); R qvalue::qvalue for \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=\textquotedbl{}storey\textquotedbl{}} and \code{\textquotedbl{}local fdr\textquotedbl{}} (Bioconductor, simplydata[r])}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:compare-shape-to]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}shape\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-spreads-of]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}spreads\_\allowbreak{}of}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-counts-of]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}counts\_\allowbreak{}of}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-counts-to]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}counts\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:compare-average-to]{\code{compare\_\allowbreak{}average\_\allowbreak{}to}}}
\where{Manual \manualpage{word:table.add-adjusted-p-value-column}{335}{section*.204}; lesson 14 (\manualpage{lesson:14}{85}{chapter.II.14})}
\headword{add\_axes\_that\_separate\_groups}{dict:add-axes-that-separate-groups}
\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}axes\_\allowbreak{}that\_\allowbreak{}separate\_\allowbreak{}groups()}}
\means{Add the axes that separate groups most (linear discriminant analysis), in new columns LD1, LD2.}

\field{Options}{\code{columns=}, \code{for\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}group\_\allowbreak{}in=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}}

\headword{add\_change\_column}{dict:add-change-column}
\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}change\_\allowbreak{}column()}}
\means{Add a column with the change from the row before: this value minus the previous one.}

                          for\_\allowbreak{}each\_\allowbreak{}group\_\allowbreak{}in=\textquotedbl{}country\textquotedbl{},\allowbreak{} sorted\_\allowbreak{}by=\textquotedbl{}year\textquotedbl{})}}

\headword{add\_clusters}{dict:add-clusters}
\sense{table}{\code{table.\allowbreak{}add\_\allowbreak{}clusters()}}

\sense{system}{\code{system.\allowbreak{}impulse\_\allowbreak{}response()}}
\means{How the output answers a short kick at time 0 (an impulse of size 1).}
\eg{\code{system.\allowbreak{}impulse\_\allowbreak{}response(until=10)}}
\field{Options}{\code{until=}, \code{how\_\allowbreak{}many=}, \code{time\_\allowbreak{}points=}}
\field{Underneath}{SciPy (signal.lti / dlti, step, impulse, lsim, freqresp, freqz, cont2discrete, tf2ss, tf2zpk); the formula read with Python's ast and NumPy polynomials; rise time, settling time, overshoot and margins from python-control (\code{step\_\allowbreak{}info}, \code{stability\_\allowbreak{}margins}: simplydata[systems])}
\field{See also}{\hyperref[dict:step-response]{\code{step\_\allowbreak{}response}}, \hyperref[dict:response-to]{\code{response\_\allowbreak{}to}}, \hyperref[dict:system]{\code{system}}, \hyperref[dict:frequency-response]{\code{frequency\_\allowbreak{}response}}, \hyperref[dict:make-window-shape]{\code{make\_\allowbreak{}window\_\allowbreak{}shape}}}

\field{Options}{\code{time\_\allowbreak{}step=}, \code{test\_\allowbreak{}method=}}

\clearpage\section*{Coming from another tool?}\label{other:names}
Names from pandas, Polars, R, NumPy, SciPy, matplotlib and seaborn, and everyday maths words. In simplydata they never run: \code{sdata.\allowbreak{}help(\textquotedbl{}groupby\textquotedbl{})} (or typing \code{table.\allowbreak{}groupby()}) points to the simplydata word. Here each name points to the word and the manual page that explains it. A name that is also a simplydata word is written with its object in front, such as \code{table.\allowbreak{}table}.
\begin{dictcolumns}
\letterhead{A}
\othername{aalen\_johansen}{\hyperref[dict:find-risk-over-time]{\code{table.\allowbreak{}find\_\allowbreak{}risk\_\allowbreak{}over\_\allowbreak{}time()}}, \manualpage{word:table.find-risk-over-time}{450}{section*.298}}
\othername{design.ab}{\hyperref[dict:make-design-table]{\code{sdata.\allowbreak{}make\_\allowbreak{}design\_\allowbreak{}table()}}, \manualpage{word:sdata.make-design-table}{498}{section*.348}}
\othername{abe}{\hyperref[dict:compare-averages-of]{\code{table.\allowbreak{}compare\_\allowbreak{}averages\_\allowbreak{}of()}}, \manualpage{word:table.compare-averages-of}{321}{section*.198}}
